svg.title: The dihydrorhodamine test for chronic granulomatous disease
svg.desc: Neutrophils are loaded with dihydrorhodamine and stimulated; the respiratory burst of the NADPH oxidase oxidises the dye to fluorescent rhodamine, which a flow cytometer measures. Normal neutrophils all shift to bright fluorescence; in chronic granulomatous disease they do not shift; an X-linked carrier has two populations.
